newsitem.title: JORDAN: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --
JORDAN, July 5 - Aqaba - Three vessels loading at berth, 6 discharging at berth. 5 Vessels waiting at anchorage to load, 3 waiting at anchorage to discharge, 1 awaiting orders.

MOZAMBIQUE, July 7 - Nacala - Port working normally. No restrictions on berthing and sailing during night time. Draft restrictions 9.5 metres at general cargo berth and 14 metres at container berth. One tug available. Beira - General cargo berths - Working normally. Container terminal/other terminals - Working normally, 24 hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 140 metres loa. Some restrictions for large vessels and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. Maximum draft for 24 hour navigation 7.5 metres. Two tugs available.

General access channel - Two wave-rider buoys have been deployed in the approach channel as follows wmon1 19 deg. 66.0460 s 36 deg. 01.6698 e and wmon2 19 deg. 62.6370 s 34 deg. 62.6497 e. Each buoy has an approximate diameter of 1 metre, with flashing orange light with a flash frequency of five one-second flashes every 36 seconds. Maputo - 24 Hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 120 metres loa. Some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. All berths working normally and expected to remain so. Draft restriction in the channel is 9.0 metres less 0.5 metres (ukc) plus the rise of tide. Maximum draft for 24 hour navigation is 9 metres.
NAMIBIA, July 7 - Walvis Bay - Port working normally.

SOUTH AFRICA, July 7 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths - Working normally. Bulk import berths - Working normally, but berth 701 experiencing some problems with clogged filters when discharging petcoke. Bulk export berths (minerals etc.) - Working normally at present, all dust protectors have been repaired. Bulk coal berths - 4 Vessels berthed, 2 at anchorage and 1 due 7/7. A further 18 vessels are due up to and including 14/7. Berthing delays of approx. 2-3 days are being experienced at present. Durban - Container terminal - Delays of up to 48 hours can be expected whilst 2 new noel cranes are being positioned. Point/New Pier/Maydon Wharf berths - Working normally for general cargo vessels. Maize terminal (Maydon Wharf 8) - 3 Vessels expected for July. Bunker supplies - Working normally, but could change daily due to bunching of vessels. Dry-dock/floating dock - Fully committed for July and August.

East London - General cargo/combi terminal/tanker berths - Busy, but no delays expected at this stage. Dry-dock - Fully booked until 20 September, thereafter open for bookings. Copper - 2,500 Metric tonnes moving out per month. Tankers - 2 Expected weekly. Scrap steel - 4,500 Metric tonnes on hand. Port Elizabeth - Working normally, with 7 vessels in port. No delays expected on general, ore or tanker berths. Fruit berth - 2 Vessels in port and 2 anchored. Container berth - 2 Vessels in port, with berthing delays of 10-12 hours experienced 9 and 10 July. Cape Town - Breakbulk berths (general cargo) - Working normally. Fruit berths - Fully occupied. Container terminal - Working normally, with vessels operating on arrival. Bunker berths - Vessels berthing and bunkering on arrival. Dry-docks and repair quays - Fully occupied, booking is essential. Saldanha Bay - Port working normally.

TUNISIA, July 5 - Gabes - No labour problems. One vessel loading bagged di-calcium phosphate at berth, no vessels anchored. Sousse - One vessel in port discharging bagged sugar. No delays, no vessels awaiting orders. Sfax - Five vessels in port operating of which 2 discharging (1 timber, 1 steel). 3 Loading (1 bulk rock phosphate, 2 tuna fish). Bizerte - July 8 - No berthing delays/congestion/strikes. Five vessels operating of which 2 discharging steel, 1 loading clinker, 1 discharging marble, 1 discharging benzene.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, June 29-5 July - Dubai - 202 Vessels of which 89 containers, 12 general cargo, 2 general cargo/containers, 4 bulk carriers, 4 car carriers, 13 tankers, 1 livestock carrier, 4 naval vessels, 5 U.A.E. naval vessels, 10 taking bunkers/stores/under repair etc., 11 dhows, 14 barges, 11 tugs, 14 supply boats, 2 passenger vessels, 1 lpg tanker, 1 frigerator vessel, 2 fishing trawlers, 1 yacht, 1 bulk oiler. July 5 - No labour problems. Three vessels loading at berth (2 containers, 1 general cargo). 12 Vessels discharging at berth (8 general cargo, 4 tankers). 3 Vessels waiting at anchorage to discharge (1 containers, 1 general cargo, 1 tanker). 10 Vessels under repair/laid-up (3 general cargo, 7 tankers). 52 Vessels due (30 containers, 15 general cargo, 7 bulkers).

YEMEN, July 6 - Hodeidah - Six vessels berthed of which 1 flour, 1 bulk wheat, 2 containers, 1 general cargo, 1 pipes. 1 Flour vessel anchored awaiting berth. Berthing delays, containers 1 day. No delays for reefers, general cargo, bagged cargo, bulk wheat/corn.
